A heuristic evaluation of the Bewakoof shopping app: a structured review of what's working and what isn't across a high-traffic ecommerce funnel.A heuristic evaluation of the Bewakoof shopping app: a structured review of what's working and what isn't across a high-traffic ecommerce funnel.

The challenge

Bewakoof is a high-traffic shopping app. The aim was to:

  • Find where its funnel creates friction
  • Do it quickly, before any costly user testing

The approach

A heuristic evaluation: an expert review of the interface against Nielsen's 10 usability heuristics. Each issue is shown as the current screen next to a proposed fix.

The details

The screens in focus:

  • Home: stories row (Specials, Shop Now, Plus Size, Accessories) and promotional banners
  • Offer cards such as "Joggers, buy 2 at ₹1699"
  • New Arrivals and product discovery
  • Bottom navigation: Men, Categories, Studio, Profile

An independent review. Not affiliated with Bewakoof.

My role

Design process

ScopePick the key screens of the funnel
ReviewCheck each against the 10 heuristics
RateRank the issues by severity
ProposeShow the current screen next to a fix
PresentLay out the findings board by board
how it landed

OutcomeOutcome

An independent review of a live app, so these are the checks I would use to confirm the fixes.

What I delivered

  • A review of the app against Nielsen's 10 heuristics
  • Severity-rated issues across the home, offers, new arrivals and navigation
  • Prioritised recommendations

How I’d measure success

  • Task success when finding and applying an offer
  • Time to reach a category from the home screen
  • The same issues re-checked after changes, with users

What it shows

  • A critical, structured eye for usability
  • Prioritising problems by severity
  • Presenting findings clearly and visually
